subject: Computer Networking
title: gRPC: High-Performance APIs
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on gRPC: High-Performance APIs.

hook.text: REST APIs send JSON text. That's human-readable but wasteful for machines talking to machines at high speed.

buildup.text: gRPC uses Protocol Buffers — a compact binary format — and HTTP/2 for multiplexed, bidirectional streaming.

discovery.text: You define your API in a .proto file. gRPC generates client and server code in dozens of languages automatically.

twist.text: gRPC supports streaming: server-stream, client-stream, and bidirectional. REST can't match that natively.

climax.text: Microservices at Google, Netflix, and many cloud platforms use gRPC for fast internal communication.

punchline.text: gRPC is built for speed between services, not humans.

quiz.question: What serialization format does gRPC use instead of JSON?

details.summary: gRPC is a high-performance remote procedure call framework that uses Protocol Buffers for serialization and HTTP/2 for transport. It supports unary calls, server streaming, client streaming, and bidirectional streaming, making it ideal for microservice communication where low latency matters.
details.whyItMatters: gRPC is the dominant protocol for internal microservice communication in modern architectures. Its binary serialization and HTTP/2 streaming deliver performance that JSON-based REST cannot match.
takeaways: Protocol Buffers serialize data in a compact binary format
HTTP/2 streaming enables four communication patterns
Strong typing with generated code catches API errors at compile time

faq.question: When should you use gRPC instead of REST?
faq.answer: Use gRPC for internal service-to-service communication where performance matters, when you need streaming, or when strong typing is valuable. Use REST for public APIs, browser-facing endpoints, and when human readability of requests is important. Many systems use gRPC internally and REST externally.

faq.question: Can browsers use gRPC directly?
faq.answer: Browsers cannot make native gRPC calls because they lack HTTP/2 trailer support. gRPC-Web is a variant that works in browsers with a proxy. Alternatively, many teams expose REST or GraphQL APIs to browsers while using gRPC between backend services.
